name: MCP-Atlas
description: MCP-Atlas is a large-scale benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool use. It indexes real MCP servers and their exposed tools/resources/prompts, then scores an agent on end-to-end tasks that require discovering the relevant server, selecting the correct tool, constructing a well-formed tool call, handling multi-turn MCP responses, and composing results across servers. Tasks span developer tooling, data access, productivity, and web automation servers, and are graded on tool-selection accuracy, argument correctness, and final task success. The benchmark is designed to stress realistic MCP workflows rather than synthetic function-calling toy tasks.
reputation: Emerging benchmark tracking the MCP ecosystem; one of the first large-scale public evaluations focused specifically on Model Context Protocol agentic tool use
notes: Unrelated to the ATLAS particle-physics experiment at CERN. Evaluates agents on realistic Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions: server discovery, tool selection, argument construction, multi-turn tool responses, and cross-server composition. Metrics typically include tool-selection accuracy, argument-schema validity, and end-task success rate on held-out task sets.
